output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm-forwarding server, not from agency staff. The hardware move was reported as like-for-like. In fact 11 of 14 forwarding rules were silently skipped, including the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat suppression, and routing technical alarms to the charge phone only. Phone notifications per nurse in Pods A–C roughly doubled from 12 August and acknowledgement times doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, saw no change. Incident rates there stayed flat even with a similar share of agency staff. Core nurses and agency nurses had similar rates after the change. Bedside alarm volume was flat, which argues against acuity and the monitor update. Core nurse sick leave rose later, probably partly from the respiratory virus season. A link to the alarm load is plausible but not proven. I am fairly confident (about 85–90%). Next step: restore the rules (about 4 hours plus validation), with Clinical Engineering and the Alarm Committee signing off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't cap agency use or open performance reviews, and don't stop phone forwarding of SpO2 alarms. Also check Pod D phase 2 isn't migrated before the rules are restored.
